messages.subject: Vector Indexing Issue
parts:
Hi All

Im trying to run a hierarchical model at state and county levels. The county level parameters are to be aggregated to the state level shown in the model attached. I have a particular problem when using random vector indexing because each state has a different number of counties and a different subset of counties. I have tried creating a nimble Function and still having problems. So for example, the line below is meant to take the eta_ct parameters for county c year t and take the exponent of each  them to get the rho_cts which is indexed by county c year t in state s. 

get counties_s is an 51 by 300 array which has the county indices for each of the 51 states.
ncounties_s is the vector of the total number of counties by state s. 
t indexes the year. 

Data and Model code are attached. 

  for(s in 1:Nstates){
    for(t in 1:Nyears){
     rho_cts[getcounties_s[s,1:ncounties_s[s]],t,s] <- SumExp(eta_ct, s, ncounties_s, getcounties_s, t)
    }
  }

Any help much appreciated

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Vector Indexing Issue
parts:
Hi EN,

Thanks for the question. I am not 100% clear on what you want, but I think it might be helpful if I try to explain some of the background about nested indexing. (In NIMBLE, we only call it "random" indexing if the indices themselves are random variables in the model that may change for example by MCMC sampling. I don't think that's your case.)

In a nimbleFunction, code is imperative, what most people are familiar with, and largely supports R syntax for math and distributions. Hence, something like your line
return(exp(eta[getcounties_s[s,1:ncounties_s[s]],t]))
*should* work (meaning it should successfully compile and the compiled version should work).

In nimbleModel, code is declarative, and it must be processed at the start based on indexing to determine relationships in the directed acyclic graph of the model. Nested indexing will work, and contiguous (sequential) index blocks will work, but non-contiguous index vectors will not work, nor will nested indexing to create potentially non-contiguous index vectors.

In your code,
rho_cts[getcounties_s[s,1:ncounties_s[s]],t,s] <- SumExp(eta_ct, s, ncounties_s, getcounties_s, t)

will not work because the first index on the left-hand side (LHS) of rho_cts is getcounties_s[s,1:ncounties_s[s]]. I presume that getcounties_s is part of your constants, but you are pulling out a vector (because of 1:ncounties_s[s]) of indices that (by syntax) would be (potentially non-contiguous) indices for rho_cts. The nimbleModel machinery for constructing graphical models (DAGs) does not support that.

Based on the name "SumExp" (but I don't see a sum in the function) and your commented code (which shows "sum(exp(...))"), I am not completely clear what you want. If you are returning a scalar (sum of exponentials?) you can use nested indexing on the LHS of a declaration to put it in the right place of a non-scalar object. Alternatively you may need to consider different indexing schemes to have continuous index ranges on the LHS of any declarations.

(I also didn't see where rho_cts is subsequently used in the model, but that might be because it was giving you trouble.)

A relatively new feature that might be useful is that you can provide user-defined distributions and functions in nimbleFunctions with setup code such that they have internal member variables. See section 12.3 of the User Manual if that sounds relevant.

HTH and let us know follow-on questions.
Perry
